scenes.heading: Cellular respiration and photosynthesis
scenes.sub: From sunlight to sugar to ATP
scenes.say: Almost all the energy living things use starts as sunlight. Photosynthesis stores it in sugar, and respiration releases it as ATP. Both use a proton gradient across a membrane.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Kids going down a line of waterslides into a pool
scenes.science: Electrons pass down the ETC to oxygen, pumping H⁺
scenes.breaks: Electrons don't fall under gravity: they move to carriers with a higher affinity for electrons, and that redox step releases energy.
scenes.say: Picture kids on a line of waterslides ending in a pool. Electrons move down the electron transport chain the same way, and the pool is oxygen, the final electron acceptor. Cyanide closes the pool, so everything stops.

scenes.heading: Little Kids Can Eat
scenes.say: Little kids can eat. Glycolysis in the cytosol gives two ATP and two NADH. The link reaction gives two more NADH. The citric acid cycle turns twice, giving six NADH and two F A D H two. Then the electron transport chain makes most of the ATP.
scenes.caption: Little Kids Can Eat. Glycolysis in the cytosol gives 2 ATP and 2 NADH. The link reaction gives 2 more NADH. The citric acid cycle turns twice, giving 6 NADH and 2 FADH₂. Then the electron transport chain makes most of the ATP.

scenes.heading: Chemiosmosis
points: ETC pumps H⁺ into intermembrane space
H⁺ flows back through ATP synthase
scenes.say: The chain is a pump and A T P synthase is a water wheel: protons rush back through it, spinning its rotor to make ATP. NADH gives about two and a half ATP, F A D H two about one and a half. An uncoupler is a hole in the dam: energy comes out as heat.
scenes.caption: The chain is a pump and ATP synthase is a water wheel: H⁺ rush back through it, spinning its rotor to make ATP. NADH gives about 2.5 ATP, FADH₂ about 1.5. An uncoupler is a hole in the dam: energy comes out as heat.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Using 2.5 ATP per NADH and 1.5 per FADH₂, what is the maximum ATP from one glucose?
scenes.say: Check it like a receipt. Four ATP are made directly. Ten NADH times two and a half is twenty-five. Two F A D H two times one and a half is three. Total: thirty-two, often quoted as thirty to thirty-two.
scenes.caption: Check it like a receipt. 4 ATP are made directly. 10 NADH × 2.5 = 25. 2 FADH₂ × 1.5 = 3. Total: 32, often quoted as 30 to 32.

scenes.heading: Light-dependent reactions
points: II before I: PSII → PSI → NADPH
scenes.say: On the thylakoids, photosystem two splits water to replace its lost electron. So plant oxygen comes from water, not carbon dioxide. Electrons flow on to photosystem one, making NADPH, while the proton gradient makes ATP.

scenes.heading: Calvin cycle: 3-6-1-5-9-6
scenes.say: The Calvin cycle runs on three, six, one, five, nine, six. Rubisco fixes three carbon dioxide, making six G three P. One leaves to make sugar, and five rebuild three R u B P. It costs nine ATP and six NADPH.
scenes.caption: The Calvin cycle runs on 3-6-1-5-9-6. Rubisco fixes 3 CO₂, making 6 G3P. 1 leaves to make sugar, and 5 rebuild 3 RuBP. It costs 9 ATP and 6 NADPH.

points: OIL RIG: oxidation is loss of electrons
Oxygen is the final electron acceptor
scenes.say: Quick recap. Oxidation is loss, reduction is gain. Oxygen is the final electron acceptor. Glucose gives about thirty to thirty-two ATP. Plant oxygen comes from water. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Quick recap. Oxidation is loss, reduction is gain. Oxygen is the final electron acceptor. Glucose gives about 30–32 ATP. Plant O₂ comes from water. Now try the practice questions!
